title: Why Is DigitalOcean Stock Falling and is it a Buying Opportunity?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks why DigitalOcean stock is falling despite accelerating growth, and whether the drop is a buying opportunity. Management is guiding fourth-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 35%, up from 28% in the most recent quarter, and at least 50% growth in 2027, but says that growth will come at the expense of operating profit margins as it invests in capacity. He traces revenue from about $300 million in 2021 to $1 billion over the trailing twelve months, crediting agentic AI and the shift from closed to open-weight models, with customers value-maxing rather than token-maxing. The cost is margin: cash flow from operations has fallen to 31% of sales from a 39% peak, which makes investors treat the growth as investment-driven rather than organic. The shares are still up over 111% year to date but down from about $180 to about $102. He likes R&D leverage — 18.7% of revenue, down from 29% in 2022 — and a forward P/E of 55 against 50% forecast growth. His updated discounted cash flow is $122 a share against about $102, roughly 20% upside over 12 to 18 months. Having called it too expensive on 13 May, he now upgrades it. The call is DOCN — BUY at a $122 DCF, his first tracked DigitalOcean call.

calls.base_case: Management guides Q4 2026 revenue growth of 35%, up from 28% in the most recent quarter, and at least 50% growth in 2027; revenue has risen from ~$300m in 2021 to ~$1bn trailing twelve months.
calls.bull_case: Agentic AI and the shift to open-weight models are driving demand (customers value-maxing rather than token-maxing); R&D fell to 18.7% of revenue from 29% in 2022, so R&D can grow in dollars while shrinking as a share of accelerating revenue.
calls.bear_case: Growth is coming at the expense of operating margins as the company invests in capacity, so investors see it as investment-driven rather than organic; cash-flow-from-operations margin has fallen to 31% from a 39% peak.
